population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 25.5% − current 16.2% = 9.3 pts of adults (≈24.8M) used and are off now; ≈6.2 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈2.6 pts of the off-now group restarted once and stopped again, so (6.2+2.6)/25.5 ≈ 35% cycled. The share is down from 40% because ~24M first-time starters joined in two years, most of them through public programmes. Persistence on the subsidised daily oral is somewhat better than the parent's ~35% one-year figure because it is free. Current users ≈ 43.3M of ~267M adults, +17.1M since 2028. Gains came from: the new National Incretin Access Program, NIAP (+7.0M); Medicaid opt-in expansion (+5.4M); Medicare (+1.0M); cash (+3.9M). Commercial is −0.3M and gray/imported +0.2M. Income thirds of ~89M adults each: bottom 15.0% (13.4M), middle 14.5% (12.9M), top 19.1% (17.0M), which averages to 16.2%. The middle third is now the least covered relative to need. It earns too much for NIAP's 250% FPL cutoff, and it was hit hardest by employer retreat and by the tariff-driven cash increases. Age bands, weighted ~20/33/24/23%, give ≈16.2%. 65+ is up only 3 pts (8→11%) because fracture and NAION warnings slow older uptake. Off-drug: ~24.8M former users, and ~199M never-users, now concentrated in the middle third and among people under 30 without comorbidity. Pediatric: ~0.7% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 510k, of whom ~400k are adolescents 12–17 and ~110k are children 6–11 after the June 2029 approval. Medicaid/CHIP pays for most 6–11 fills under EPSDT. The oldest pediatric-exposed cohort now has ~7 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Public programmes now pay ≈49% of fills. (1) Medicare ≈6.2M users (14% of fills): Part D diabetes/CV/OSA ≈4.3M plus GLP-1 Bridge obesity ≈1.9M. The Bridge was extended in Sept 2029 through Dec 2031 on unchanged $245/$50 terms; 1.9M × $245 × 12 ≈ $5.6B/yr. (2) Medicaid ≈8.0M (18.5%): 2.6M legacy users at $245 (2.6M × 245 × 12 ≈ $7.6B, normal FMAP), plus 5.4M newly covered under the NIAP opt-in, where Washington pays 100% of the drug at the federal Foundayo contract price of $95 (5.4M × 95 × 12 ≈ $6.2B). 31 states plus DC have opted in. Indiana and Arkansas keep their adherence-gated waivers. (3) NIAP ≈7.0M (16%): free Foundayo for adults 18–64 at ≤250% FPL with BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity, who have no obesity drug coverage. It is dispensed through FQHCs and contracted pharmacies. Cost: 7.0M × ($95 drug + $10 dispensing) × 12 ≈ $8.8B against a $9.0B FY2030 appropriation, so new enrolment was waitlisted from Nov 2030. CHIP/EPSDT covers most pediatric fills.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ generic semaglutide brands at $8–45/month domestically. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 80–110. Generics also sell in China, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey, and generic oral semaglutide in ~170 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Price shock up. Section 232 pharma tariffs took effect Jan 2029 (25% rising to 100% by 2030 on branded imports from firms without qualifying US capacity). Novo's injectable semaglutide, made with Danish API, went from $349 to $499 cash. Lilly raised Zepbound vials from $299–449 to $399–549 and retatrutide's list from $1,499 to $1,649. Oral starting doses (Foundayo and the Wegovy pill, both US-made) held at $149, but Foundayo maintenance doses are $299. Mail-order imports fell after the Apr 2029 end of personal-importation discretion for incretin parcels. Reshipped Indian pens now cost $60–120 to the buyer, and gray use is ≈1.5M despite seizures. Payer mix of ~43.3M users: commercial 11.5M (26.6%), Medicare 6.2M (14.3%), Medicaid 8.0M (18.5%), NIAP 7.0M (16.2%), cash 9.1M (21.0%), gray 1.5M (3.5%), totalling 43.3M. Employer coverage for weight management is down from 58% to 44%. Commercial plans have re-coded toward diabetes, CVD, OSA, MASH, CKD and the March 2029 smoking-cessation indication. ACA preventive-services rules make the cessation indication zero-cost for up to two 90-day quit attempts a year, under medical management (concurrent NRT/varenicline, sometimes a cotinine test). The result is a two-tier system: weight-only patients in the middle third pay cash or cycle.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro), incl. 'Zepbound Strong' bundled programme
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2029)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Aug 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking cessation adjunct with NRT/varenicline (semaglutide/Wegovy, Mar 2029)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health'/longevity low-dose orals in people without obesity, mostly top-third cash
alcohol reduction, incl. EAP referrals, now less often employer-paid
use of the cessation indication by light or occasional nicotine users to get zero-cost coverage (anecdotal and contested by plans)
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Approvals in this window: survodutide (Feb 2029; under review at start), amycretin (Aug 2029; filed Jun 2028), Wegovy smoking-cessation sNDA (Mar 2029), Wegovy ages 6–11 (Jun 2029). MariTide (monthly) has reported phase 3 data; filing is planned for 2031 and it is not on the market. Muscle-preserving combination: bimagrumab + tirzepatide entered phase 3 in mid-2029, with readout no earlier than 2031, so it is NOT on the US market. Under the envelope rules the driver is realised as an existing product in a new form. In Nov 2029 Zepbound's label added body-composition data from a 72-week trial in which tirzepatide plus supervised resistance training and a protein protocol cut the lean share of loss from ~35% to ~20%. In Mar 2030 Lilly launched 'Zepbound Strong' through LillyDirect: tirzepatide vials, a Lilly-branded medical-food protein/leucine supplement, DEXA every 6 months and app-plus-trainer coaching, at $649/month cash. It is marketed as 'muscle-protected weight loss'. FDA's OPDP sent an untitled letter (Aug 2030) over claims implying a drug-level muscle benefit. Incretin market ≈$128B in 2030: volume up sharply but at lower average net price, since NIAP/Medicaid oral at $95 dilutes the mix.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of discontinuation; drug holidays add re-escalation GI episodes.
Elevated with rapid loss; salient with retatrutide and amycretin.
No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low.
Lean share of loss is ~25–40% without intervention and ~20% with supervised training. Most NIAP and cash-oral users get no body-composition assessment.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class label recommendations retained. Zepbound label adds body-composition data (Nov 2029). OPDP untitled letter on 'muscle-protected' marketing (Aug 2030).

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 for hip/vertebral fracture in 65+ long-term users, concentrated in women and in cyclers. Data on drug holidays are absent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class BMD labelling and DEXA recommendation for 65+ and postmenopausal women. Senate HELP report issued 2029. DOJ settlement talks with Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pooled Sentinel, claims and trial analyses (2029) give HR ~1.8–2.2 in sustained users, higher with OSA, crowded optic discs and rapid glycaemic drops. At current use that is on the order of a few thousand excess cases a year nationally; absolute individual risk remains low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class Warning & Precaution across all GLP-1-receptor-agonist-containing products (Aug 2029): baseline eye exam for those at risk, stop on sudden vision loss. Moved up from EMA's 'very rare' tier. Mass-tort filings consolidated in an MDL (2030).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in regulator or systematic-review data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the flats')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: An interim retatrutide postmarketing analysis (2030) using a validated anhedonia scale finds a small, dose-dependent rise in scores. Surveys still put self-reported reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users. Dose reduction and drug holidays are common responses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change; FDA has asked all sponsors for anhedonia-scale data.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial within a year. Now driven by employer coverage loss, 90-day cessation course limits, Indiana/Arkansas lockouts and NIAP waitlists.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; Indiana waiver litigation unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein insufficiency persist, especially in high-loss and low-income users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional society guidance; no formal requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents and now children 6–11 who may take these for decades; effects of repeated cycling and drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exist. Bone-accrual and pubertal-timing data in 6–11s are absent at approval.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Wegovy 6–11 approval carries PMRs for bone accrual, growth and puberty, plus a pediatric registry.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: After the import crackdown, counterfeit pens sold through social-media resellers are the main source of harm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion; personal-importation discretion ended for incretins (Apr 2029); parcel seizures.

safety_ledger.effect: Harms from unapproved 'muscle adjuncts' (SARMs, myostatin 'research peptides') taken alongside incretins
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case reports of liver injury and lipid derangement from online 'lean stack' products, mostly among cash and gray users trying to copy the Strong bundle.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to sellers; no import alert specific to the class.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure resumes and moves down-market. Bottom-third uptake doubled, so discount and dollar-store channels report the sharpest snack and soda declines (low-to-mid single digits by volume in 2030). Packaged-food makers shrink pack sizes and push protein and 'GLP-1 friendly' lines priced for SNAP baskets. Premium protein and dairy keep growing in the top third.

alcohol.state: Still contracting. The cessation indication, combined with the ACA zero-cost rule, brings in a large nicotine cohort whose drinking also falls. Beer and value spirits are hit hardest as the user base becomes more working-class. Tobacco and nicotine-pouch volumes fall, and makers cite the indication in guidance.

restaurants.state: Small plates and protein-forward menus are the norm. Value QSR chains report traffic softness in NIAP-dense counties. Upscale restaurants sell 'strength plates' by protein gram.

apparel.state: Sizes bifurcate by class. Fitted athletic and 'shoulder-cut' tailoring sells to the top. Stretch and wide size runs serve middle-income customers who are cycling. Plus-size has stabilised.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains, the Strong bundle's trainer network, and Medicare Advantage strength benefits. Visible muscle is a paid service, and gym membership mix skews further toward the top third.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down from 58% to 44%. Plans re-code toward diabetes/cardiac/OSA and the cessation indication, and fight ACA zero-cost claims with medical management. Large-employer pharmacy trend has eased to ~+6%. The cost has shifted to cash-paying members and to federal programmes.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates: US-made Foundayo won the NIAP contract and is exempt from the tariffs. Novo absorbs tariffs, raises cash prices, loses share and announces new North Carolina capacity for 2031. Volume is up sharply while average net price falls.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Shape now reads as payer. Lean with visible muscle means cash, DEXA and a trainer. Thin and soft, the 'program body', means free pills without monitoring. A body whose weight visibly swings means a middle-income job whose plan dropped coverage. People say 'coverage weight' about regain.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness alone no longer marks class, because the bottom third now has free oral access. Muscle is the uniform. Local case: among women teachers aged 35–55 in Gwinnett County, Georgia, the state health benefit plan's January 2030 exclusion of weight-only coverage left most of them earning too much for NIAP and unable to comfortably pay $299–549. Staff-room talk is about the 90-day cessation course, the $149 starting dose and who has regained. Ten miles away, the lunch crowd at Buckhead finance offices orders by protein gram.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller shared meals and protein-first eating are standard. School cafeterias now see 6–11-year-olds on Wegovy, and some districts have 'small-appetite' lunch protocols. Hosts plan for on, off and holiday guests.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state on/off and, increasingly, 'holiday weekends'. Visible muscle is a dating-market signal of income. Couples coordinate dose holidays around anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still treated as something to manage, but the complaint culture has softened that. Wanting things again on a drug holiday is talked about as a small luxury, the way people talk about sleeping in.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure; an interim validated-scale signal (2030) is small and dose-dependent. Practices are widespread: an estimated quarter to a third of oral users skip doses on weekends or around events, and tapering to the lowest effective dose is routine advice in telehealth scripts. The 90-day cessation courses and NIAP waitlists add involuntary holidays.
interior_life.framing: Mainstream language is 'the flats' and 'taking a holiday'. Clinicians call it dose-dependent reward modulation and manage it like a side effect. The cessation indication sells the same mechanism as treatment. Employers have stopped marketing 'even-keel' outcomes as they withdraw coverage.
interior_life.effect_on_work: With coverage shrinking, adherence no longer tracks employment as tightly, except in trucking, where tirzepatide for OSA meets the NAION warning. FMCSA medical-examiner guidance (2030) asks about visual symptoms, and drivers weigh apnea clearance against eye risk. Sales and creative workers routinely schedule dose-light weeks before pitches.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' is a genre: songs, stand-up sets and dinner parties are timed to drug holidays. Festivals advertise as 'off-dose friendly'. Some studios book recording sessions on holiday weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire complaints are now ordinary. Couples plan holidays together. Sex therapists and OB-GYNs ask about dose schedules at intake.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The fight is over cost tiers, not temperament. 'Missing middle' teachers and nurses become a campaign constituency against tariffs and for NIAP expansion. Conservatives split between deficit hawks attacking NIAP's $9B and populists defending it. India trade talks feature the parcel crackdown. There is still no measured effect on turnout or mood.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on approvals (survodutide, amycretin, cessation, ages 6–11), defensive on safety (NAION class warning, pediatric PMRs, OPDP enforcement on muscle claims), and hard on imports since the end of personal-importation discretion.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy. NIAP (FY2030 appropriation, $9.0B) gives free Foundayo to eligible low-income adults, and Medicaid opt-in states get 100% federal drug funding for new obesity enrollees. The Medicare Bridge is extended through 2031 on unchanged terms. There is no mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Indiana and Arkansas keep 80% PDC plus quarterly kiosk weigh-in gating. NIAP has no federal adherence gate but requires annual recertification, a weigh-in at enrolment and inclusion in an HRSA enrolment registry, and privacy groups object to the registry's retention terms. Employer gating has faded as coverage is withdrawn. BMI-linked wellness surcharges persist at plans that still cover.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT drivers face conflicting incentives between OSA clearance and NAION. The Army still permits GLP-1 use for recruits who meet standards, and NIAP has enlarged the eligible pool in recruiting-heavy southern counties.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs reward domestic manufacturing (Lilly) and penalise Danish-sourced supply (Novo). Denmark and the EU protest. The parcel crackdown is an irritant in US–India trade talks. Retatrutide is no longer allocated after Lilly's Concord plant came online in 2030.

events.event: Section 232 tariffs on branded pharmaceutical imports take effect. Novo lifts the Wegovy injectable cash price from $349 to $499 and Lilly raises Zepbound vials by $100 and retatrutide's list to $1,649, while US-made oral starting doses hold at $149. In April FDA and CBP end personal-importation discretion for incretin parcels, and seizures of Indian pens multiply

FDA approves Wegovy for children 6–11 with obesity, the first incretin cleared under age 12, with postmarketing requirements on bone accrual, growth and puberty; Medicaid programmes begin covering it under EPSDT

Citing pooled Sentinel and trial data showing roughly a doubling of NAION risk in sustained users, FDA adds a class Warning & Precaution for optic-nerve injury to every GLP-1-receptor-agonist-containing product and advises baseline eye exams for patients at risk

Annual benefit surveys show employer coverage of weight-only GLP-1 use falling from 58% to 44% for the 2030 plan year, led by state employee plans in Georgia, North Carolina and Colorado. Plans restrict to diabetes, cardiac, sleep-apnea and the new smoking-cessation codes

Congress funds a $9B National Incretin Access Program in the FY2030 omnibus. HHS signs a $95-a-month contract with Lilly for Foundayo, dispensed free from January through health centres and pharmacies to adults under 250% of poverty, with full federal payment for states that add obesity coverage to Medicaid. Enrolment reaches 7 million and is waitlisted by November 2030

Lilly launches 'Zepbound Strong', a $649-a-month cash bundle of tirzepatide, a branded protein supplement, twice-yearly DEXA and trainer coaching, after a label update showing lean-mass loss roughly halved with supervised training. FDA later tells Lilly its 'muscle-protected' ads overstate the drug's role, and the bimagrumab combination stays in phase 3

open_tensions: NIAP has made the bottom third the fastest-growing user group, on free pills with none of the DEXA, eye-exam or strength monitoring the labels now recommend. Monitored, muscle-protected use is a $649 cash product. Class shows in bodies, and the programme's $9B cap is already binding.

The middle third, dropped by employers and priced up by tariffs, is managing access through 90-day cessation courses, $149 starting doses and involuntary holidays. That is exactly the repeated cycling pattern the bone data flag and nobody has studied.

The NAION class warning sits against a trucking workforce steered onto tirzepatide for sleep-apnea clearance, and against 6–11-year-olds who may take the drugs for sixty years with no bone-accrual data yet.

'Muscle-protected' weight loss is sold as solved before any muscle-preserving drug has read out phase 3. Meanwhile 'the flats' is a mainstream complaint whose self-prescribed treatment, the drug holiday, has never been studied for safety.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it; the tariff increase came through cash and direct channels.
Medicare's GLP-1 Bridge still pays ~$245 a month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay on the same BMI/comorbidity criteria, now extended through 2031.

Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and a quarterly verified weigh-in; missing two checks ends coverage for 12 months, and the disability-rights litigation is unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Free Pills for the Poor, Muscle for the Rich, and a Bill for Everyone in Between
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 about one American adult in six is on an incretin drug, some forty-three million people, up from one in ten two years ago. The growth did not come from falling prices. It came from Washington. In the December 2029 spending bill Congress funded a nine-billion-dollar National Incretin Access Program, and HHS signed a contract with Lilly for its US-made pill, Foundayo, at ninety-five dollars a month. From January, adults below two and a half times the poverty line who had no other coverage could pick it up free at a health centre or a pharmacy counter. Seven million did so within the year, and five million more came in through Medicaid in the thirty-one states that took the offer of full federal payment. By November the money was running out and new applicants were put on a waitlist.

For almost everyone else, prices rose. Section 232 tariffs reached imported branded drugs in January 2029. Novo Nordisk, still making semaglutide from Danish ingredients, raised its cash price for the injectable from $349 to $499, and Lilly added a hundred dollars to its vials. The cheap escape route closed that spring when federal agencies stopped tolerating personal imports of incretins, and parcels of Indian pens began to be seized. At the same time employers kept withdrawing. Fewer than half now cover weight management at all. Georgia's state employee plan was among the first to drop weight-only coverage for 2030, and plans everywhere moved coverage to diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea and, after a March 2029 approval, smoking cessation. Because of an Affordable Care Act rule, the cessation indication is free for two ninety-day quit attempts a year, and many middle-income users now plan their year around those two windows.

The result is easiest to see in bodies. The bottom third, once the least medicated, now uses the drugs at about the national rate, mostly as a daily pill with no bone scan, no eye exam and no trainer. The top third pays cash for something different. Lilly's Zepbound Strong bundle combines the injection with a protein supplement, twice-yearly body scans and coaching, sells for $649 a month, and is advertised as weight loss that spares muscle. The FDA told Lilly the ads overstate what the drug itself does; the actual muscle-preserving drug, a bimagrumab combination, will not read out until 2031 at the earliest. Even so, broad shoulders have become the sign of money, thin and soft has become the sign of the programme, and a body that gains and loses with each plan year belongs to a teacher or a nurse in the middle. Among women teachers in Gwinnett County, Georgia, the staff room has a word for regain: coverage weight.

The labels now carry more warnings. In August 2029 the FDA put optic-nerve injury on every drug in the class, about a doubling of a rare kind of sudden vision loss. That alarmed truck drivers whose fleets had moved them onto tirzepatide to pass sleep-apnea screening, and it reached families just as Wegovy was approved that June for children as young as six. The bone and muscle warnings for older adults stand. None of this has slowed approvals: survodutide and amycretin both reached the market in 2029.

The drugs' quieting effect is no longer a niche finding. People call it the flats. A new postmarketing analysis found a small, dose-dependent signal on a validated scale, and the response has been practical rather than political. Users skip weekend doses, taper before weddings and pitches, and book recording sessions and anniversaries for their drug holidays. Nobody has studied what repeated holidays do to bone. From the outside the country looks healthier, and on most measures it is. The open question is what the programme body, the coverage weight and a six-year-old's sixty-year prescription will add up to.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Albright wakes at 5:40 in Lawrenceville and does the injection before coffee. Week ten of twelve. The pharmacy sticker says SMOKING CESSATION – $0.00, and she does use the pouches, mostly in the car. After December it's the Foundayo starting dose, $149, on the card she keeps for gas.

At the light on Sugarloaf she covers her left eye, then her right. Both fine. She doesn't remember when she started doing that.

First period, eighth-grade science, cell respiration. A girl in the back row eats nothing at lunch but half a protein pouch, and Renee knows from the 504 plan that it isn't a diet. In the staff room Carla says she's taking the weekend off for her daughter's quinceañera. 'I want to want the cake,' she says. Someone laughs. Someone asks Renee if she's regaining yet, and she says not yet, and holds her sleeve where her arm used to be.

Her sister calls from Macon on the drive home. The clinic gave her the pill free and weighed her in front of the receptionist, and her husband is on a waitlist now. 'They said spring.'

At Kroger the endcap of Takis is half the length it was. A screen by the pharmacy shows a woman with shoulders like a swimmer: STRONG. MUSCLE-PROTECTED. $649/MONTH.

At home she does twenty push-ups against the kitchen counter while the rice cooks. She eats six bites, then two more because she can. She sets an alarm for the next shot, and another for December.
